snippet.title: Doomsday: 7 Days To Prepare Before Everything Collapses
snippet.description:
#doomsday #survival #emergencypreparedness 

You have seven days to prepare before everyday systems begin breaking down. This doomsday survival story follows one ordinary person as payment networks fail, power outages spread, running water becomes unreliable, fuel deliveries slow, and the city gradually loses the systems everyone depends on.    

Instead of panic-buying, the focus is on practical emergency preparedness: storing water, managing food, conserving fuel, protecting battery power, reducing waste, and separating useful information from noise. As each day passes, preparation becomes less about owning more supplies and more about making smart decisions before stress takes over.

By Day 7, electricity and running water are gone, communications are fading, and emergency distribution sites are being established. Yet careful preparation has created something just as important as food or batteries—the ability to stay calm, conserve resources, and wait safely when normal systems stop working.  

#collapsepreparedness #disastersurvival #survivalstory #doomsdayprepping

snippet.title: | YEAR ONE |  Couple Builds Log Cabin Alone on Remote Island
snippet.description:
In our first year we ended up doing about 40 trips to the island and spent well over 100 nights there.

This was our first year on the island! It definitely had its ups and downs but if you told me before this all started we'd have cut down so many trees and built as much as we have so far I would not have believed you!

From nothing to an island tiny home, can't wait for year 2!

More about us, the island and the process:

The island is completely secluded, has no electricity or plumbing and had nothing on it when we bought it so far we have built a mini log cabin, outhouse, tent platform and a barge. We want to turn this island into a fully functioning summer cottage with a log cabin, sauna and other amenities. of The lake freezes in the winter and the weather conditions are tough hopefully the mini cabin makes it a bit easier to build all year long. 

There's a lot of work to be done as the island is over 2.5 acres (1 hectare) and we have no experience in off-grid living, carpentry or building. So any tips or advice are greatly appreciated, as we are planning on doing everything ourselves and transforming the island into our own little paradise. We’ll document every step of the way, starting from smaller builds to finally - an off-grid log cabin.

snippet.title: 16 Breakfast Foods To STOCKPILE That NEVER EXPIRE!
snippet.description:
Most people think they're preparing for the future by stockpiling food. But what if the foods you're storing are the ones most likely to spoil first? In this video, we reveal 16 surprisingly long-lasting breakfast foods that can stay fresh for years—and in some cases, decades—when stored correctly. From pantry staples to forgotten survival foods, these are the items smart preppers keep on hand.

What most people miss is that long-term food storage isn't just about calories. It's about nutrition, shelf life, convenience, and building a system that actually works when you need it. We'll cover the best grains, proteins, natural sweeteners, and even one living food source that can produce fresh nutrients right from your kitchen.

The reality is that many common breakfast foods fail because of hidden ingredients, poor storage methods, or simple misinformation. Understanding which foods last—and why—can save money, reduce waste, and help create a more reliable emergency food supply.

Disclaimer: This video is for educational and informational purposes only. Food shelf life depends on storage conditions, packaging, and product quality.

In this video, we break down 10 essential EMP-proof survival tools and off-grid prepping essentials that keep working long after every phone, car, and appliance around you goes dead. From solar garden lights and cast iron cookware to manual water filtration, hand tools, and printed survival manuals, this is the ultimate blackout survival gear list for anyone serious about emergency preparedness, SHTF planning, and grid-down survival.

We cover real-world case studies — including the Venezuela blackout, Hurricane Maria in Puerto Rico, the Siege of Sarajevo, Argentina's 2001 economic collapse, and the 2010 Haiti earthquake — to show exactly why low-tech, zero-electronics gear consistently outperforms modern tech during a long-term power outage or EMP attack. Whether you're building a bug-out bag, stocking a survival pantry, or just starting your prepper journey, this video gives you a practical, no-nonsense checklist of gear that works with zero batteries, zero circuits, and zero dependency on the grid.

If you're into emergency preparedness, self-reliance, homesteading, and off-grid living, this is the channel for you. Emergency preparedness has a problem.

Not because people do not care.
Not because they are lazy.

This episode explores:

Why “all-hazards preparedness” can overwhelm the public
Why people often default to Google, Facebook, or social media during emergencies
How stress affects decision-making during a crisis
Why preparedness tools need to be accessible and easy to understand

Real-world stories where simple guidance helped people make better emergency decisions
Why preparedness is not just about information — it is about human behavior, trust, and interaction
How communities can make preparedness more social, practical, and empowering

Preparedness should not make people feel afraid.
It should make people feel capable.

In this episode it's just me and the kids learning as we go to install the flooring in our off-grid cabin here on the Kenai Peninsula, Alaska. And of course, right in the middle of flooring day our generator starts acting up.

You'll see us figure out flooring for the first time, troubleshoot the generator.

Thank you for following our family's journey from South Carolina back home to Alaska as we build our homestead from scratch. We had a door, lights, insulation, windows and sheetrock for move-in night — now we finally have a real floor!

Next up: plumbing, so this little cabin really works for our family of six.

Watch how it all began start to finish here: 

https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLe9yenw3s7DY&si=_goWrt7d9ng7GvG-

New here? We're Anna & Gordon and our 4 kids, building an off-grid cabin/homestead in Alaska. Subscribe to follow the build.

Extreme Heat Prepping:  How to Survive 110°F Without Power
Extreme heat can become life-threatening much faster than most people realize, especially when the power goes out. Without air conditioning, fans, or reliable refrigeration, indoor temperatures can climb rapidly, turning an ordinary home into a dangerous environment. Preparing before a heat emergency is one of the most effective ways to protect yourself and your family.

In this video, we explore practical strategies for surviving extreme heat during a prolonged power outage. We cover hydration, passive cooling techniques, home insulation, ventilation, shade, emergency water storage, cooling centers, heat illness prevention, and the supplies that experienced preppers rely on when temperatures reach 110°F or higher.

If you're interested in emergency preparedness, heat wave survival, off-grid living, disaster readiness, power outage planning, and prepping for 2026, this guide will help you build a practical plan for staying safe during extreme summer conditions.

We also explain common mistakes people make during heat emergencies, including relying on ineffective cooling methods, waiting too long to hydrate, and failing to recognize the early warning signs of heat exhaustion and heat stroke.

The best time to prepare for extreme heat is before the temperature rises. Watch until the end, because several inexpensive items and simple preparation steps can dramatically improve your ability to stay safe and comfortable during a prolonged blackout.

snippet.title: If the Grid Goes Down Tonight, Most Families Won't
snippet.description:
If the power grid goes down tonight, the biggest threat will not be the darkness itself. The real danger begins during the first 72 hours — when normal systems people depend on every day start failing one by one. Water access becomes uncertain, food supplies become limited, communication disappears, temperatures become harder to control, and simple decisions become critical.

This investigation reveals what truly happens during a prolonged blackout and why many families who believe they are prepared are actually vulnerable within just a few days. We examine the failures that happen first, the survival priorities most people overlook, and how water, food, lighting, communication, sanitation, and home security must work together as a complete emergency system.

By the end of this video, you’ll understand why preparation is not about fear — it is about having the right systems in place before a crisis begins.
